title.narrative: A global ocean free from the harmful impacts of pollution: Roadmap implementation plan

description.narrative: This project aims to develop an implementation plan for the “A global ocean free from the harmful impacts of pollution: Roadmap for action,” launched on 14th March 2024 at the World Ocean Summit in Lisbon by Back to Blue (The Economist and Nippon Foundation) with a view to present the implementation plan to the The Nippon Foundation at or ahead of the World Ocean Summit to be held in Tokyo in March 2025. IOC UNESCO and UNEP secretariats have agreed among them and with Nippon Foundation to translate the Roadmap into an implementation plan. Back to Blue has undertaken a two-year effort to engage global stakeholders on how best to close the global gap in our understanding of ocean pollution. A global ocean free from the harmful impacts of pollution: Roadmap for action, is a culmination of this endeavour. The roadmap is a strategic framework to build a comprehensive evidence base to tackle ocean pollution collectively. The overall objective is developing an implementation plan (as basis for a project document) which clarifies roles and responsibilities of the suggested lead implementation agencies, IOC UNESCO and UNEP; identifies all partners; identifies critical existing mechanisms and frameworks to coordinate with; and to develop a work plan for a decadal undertaking with defined short term (annual) and longer-term deliverables. Finally, the objective is to develop a budget for the cost of implementing the Back to Blue Road Map through the identified activities and for delivering the identified outcomes on time. The aim is a collaborative, coordinated and global approach to harmonise existing projects, catalyse new initiatives and increase momentum for action. The project initially contributes to the United Nations Decade of Ocean Science for Sustainable Development 2021-2030, and aligns with its ambition to “understand and beat marine pollution”.
